title: RWTH Aachen develops scalable manufacturing for multi-layer electrodes - electrive.com
content:
Under the ProMeBa research project, RWTH Aachen is developing scalable processes for multilayer battery electrodes. The goal is to transfer the technology from the lab to pilot scale.
Multilayer battery electrode in the ProMeBa research project.
Image: PEM RWTH Aachen
The Chair of Production Engineering of E-Mobility Components (PEM) at RWTH Aachen, together with several partners, first launched the ProMeBa research project in June 2026. The project will run until May 2029 and is being conducted as part of a German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK) scheme.
Multilayer electrodes offer significant advantages but are far more challenging to manufacture than conventional single-layer structures. ProMeBa therefore aims to demonstrate how such electrodes can be produced stably and reproducibly on an industrial scale. Differently structured layers are intended to improve ion transport, enhance the mechanical stability of the electrode, and increase the performance and lifespan of the battery.
At the beginning of the project, suitable materials and layer architectures for anodes and cathodes will be investigated. The focus will be on aspects such as the number of layers, individual layer thickness, and possible composition gradients. The derived electrode concepts will then be implemented and characterised in the laboratory using adapted slurry formulations as well as coating and drying parameters.
Multi-layer electrodes on the path to pilot scale
PEM is primarily responsible for the formulation and process development of multi-layer anodes, as well as their characterisation at laboratory scale. The insights gained will subsequently be transferred to pilot scale.
For this purpose, a modular coating module will be developed that can be integrated into existing pilot plants. Two processes will be examined under industrially relevant roll-to-roll conditions: multi-layer coating using a two-layer slot die and multi-layer curtain coating. The decisive factor is which solution combines high coating quality, stable process conditions, and good scalability.
In parallel, an inline measurement technique for the continuous determination of the viscosity of electrode slurries will be further developed. This is intended to detect deviations in the process at an early stage and ensure reproducible electrode quality.
The manufactured electrodes and test cells will also be electrochemically examined. This should provide insights into the performance, stability, and lifespan of the developed multi-layer structures.
The project coordinator is Netzsch-Gerätebau GmbH. In addition to PEM, other partners include the ISEA Chair at RWTH Aachen, Fraunhofer IKTS, the iPAT Institute at Technische Universität Braunschweig, and 8inks Deutschland.
The industrial added value lies primarily in the fact that ProMeBa not only develops new electrode structures but also considers their manufacturing from the outset. The project partners aim to create a “drop-in capable” technology that allows existing production infrastructures to be selectively expanded, rather than building entirely new production lines for multi-layer electrodes.
ProMeBa thus joins a series of research projects that more closely link material development and industrial scaling. For example, the
AIT-led MoSiLIB project
is working on a composite anode made of silicon and tin sulfide while simultaneously investigating the semi-industrial scaling of synthesis and water-based electrode manufacturing. While MoSiLIB primarily develops new anode materials, ProMeBa focuses more on the question of how complex electrode architectures can be reproducibly integrated into existing production processes.

title: BMW begins Gen6 battery production in Irlbach-Straßkirchen - electrive.com
content:
BMW has officially opened its new battery plant in Irlbach-Straßkirchen and launched series production. The site will supply sixth-generation high-voltage batteries initially for the new BMW i3 from Munich and is set to play a central role in Germany's production network in the future.
Markus Söder at the opening of the new BMW plant in Irlbach-Straßkirchen.
Image: BMW
Just two and a half years after construction began, BMW’s new plant in Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Lower Bavaria, has entered series production. Bavarian Minister-President Markus Söder attended the opening of the new facility, emphasising the importance of the location south of Regensburg for industrial value creation and electromobility in Bavaria. Due to high demand for the Neue Klasse models, BMW is ramping up the site faster than originally planned and has already begun operating in two shifts. The manufacturer is investing around one billion euros in the plant.
At launch, Irlbach-Straßkirchen is supplying the Munich plant with sixth-generation high-voltage batteries for the new BMW i3. In the future, the site is set to serve as a central hub, providing Gen6 batteries to other German vehicle plants. The production facility was built on a site covering approximately 60 hectares. Less than two years passed between the start of construction in April 2024 and the production of the first pre-series batteries in March 2026. At full capacity, around 1,600 people will work at the plant. BMW aims to produce several hundred high-voltage batteries per day across two production lines.
The new BMW site initially faced opposition in the region. It was only after a
citizen referendum in September 2023
that the way was cleared for the plant’s establishment. As early as spring 2025, BMW announced that the central
production building had been completed on schedule
and that installation of the production equipment could begin.
BMW adopts 800 volt and cell-to-pack systems for Gen6
The start of production in Irlbach-Straßkirchen is part of the broader Gen6 technology transition for the Neue Klasse. For the first time, BMW is adopting an 800-volt architecture and large-format cylindrical cells with a 46-millimetre diameter. According to BMW, these new cylindrical cells offer around 20 per cent higher energy density compared to the previous prismatic cells.
BMW opens Irlbach-Straßkirchen and starts Gen6 battery production.
The cells are integrated directly into the high-voltage battery using the cell-to-pack principle. The battery housing itself becomes part of the vehicle structure through the pack-to-open-body principle. BMW promises faster charging and greater ranges for Gen6 technology compared to Gen5.
Production in Irlbach-Straßkirchen is highly automated. Across approximately 50,000 square metres of production space, 500 robots are in use. More than 3,500 data points are recorded during the production of each battery and monitored in real time. AI-based assistance systems are used to analyse the data and ensure process quality.
Gen6 batteries
, BMW is pursuing a global “local for local” strategy. In addition to Irlbach-Straßkirchen, new assembly plants are being or have been established in Debrecen, Shenyang, Woodruff, and San Luis Potosí. The goal is to locate battery assembly as close as possible to the respective vehicle plants.
BMW sources the battery cells themselves from external cell manufacturers. At the plant, they are inspected, assembled into cell clusters, connected to coolers, and then welded. A foaming process mechanically bonds the components, increasing stability and protection. Finally, each high-voltage battery undergoes a comprehensive end-of-line inspection.
BMW also aims to improve its CO2 footprint through material usage. The Gen6 cells incorporate secondary materials for cobalt, lithium, and nickel. According to BMW, renewable energy is used in the production of anode and cathode materials as well as in cell manufacturing. This is expected to reduce CO2 emissions per watt-hour by around 33 per cent compared to Gen5 cells.
The new BMW i3 will initially use a 108.7 kWh battery from the Lower Bavarian production site. For the
i3 50 xDrive
, BMW quotes a WLTP range of up to 906 kilometres. Thanks to 800-volt technology and DC fast charging at up to 400 kW, up to 423 kilometres of range can be added in just ten minutes. The i3 also supports bidirectional charging.
The plant is part of a larger
Bavarian battery network
. Development and pilot production take place in locations such as Parsdorf, Hallbergmoos, and the Munich Research and Innovation Centre. In nearby Salching, BMW has also been operating a
competence centre for direct recycling
of battery cells and production residues since the end of 2025.

title: Toyota Battery Center of North America Unveiled at Michigan R&D Campus - Batteries News
content:
Toyota Battery Center of North America Unveiled at Michigan R&D Campus
SALINE, Mich., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — The next chapter of Toyota’s electrification transformation begins today with the opening of the Toyota Battery Center of North America (TBC) in Saline, Michigan. The new facility gives Toyota’s Michigan-based battery teams increased capabilities to evaluate and develop technology across the full battery-development cycle, from sourcing raw materials to customer applications to recycling.
Keita Moritsu,
Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, Toyota Motor North America R&D, said:
Toyota has long been at the forefront of battery development,
“This center is where that leadership expands to North America — and where we’re building its next chapter.”
The 30,000-square-foot facility serves as a central hub for development and evaluation, in partnership with Toyota’s North American manufacturing network, supporting the evaluation of batteries for Toyota Battery Manufacturing, North Carolina, as well as Toyota’s vehicle manufacturing plants across North America.
TBC also represents the latest milestone in Toyota’s more than 50-year history with the state of Michigan.
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer, said:
Today is a big win for Michigan’s leadership in advanced automotive manufacturing,
“We are proud to welcome this investment by Toyota that positions Michigan as the best place to build the future. This state-of-the-art facility will develop, test, and improve the batteries powering the next generation of vehicles. It joins factories and projects opening across our state that are creating good-paying, high-skilled jobs in every community. Let’s keep working together to build the future of cars, chips, batteries, and so much more right here in Michigan.”
TBC’s evaluation and development capabilities support Toyota’s multi-pathway strategy by enabling a range of sustainable mobility solutions for customers. On site, teams of engineers and technicians assess battery performance and develop new technologies for use in hybrid, plug-in hybrid, hydrogen, and fully electric vehicles.
Jordan Choby,
Group Vice President of Powertrain, said:
For Toyota customers, this facility means Toyota engineers can detect and resolve field concerns faster and closer to the source,
“It also means we can develop longer-lasting batteries designed to perform in the conditions American drivers face every day.”
Toyota will open the facility and research access with the University of Michigan Electric Vehicle Center, allowing other research partners to benefit from its cutting-edge testing and evaluation capabilities. As a founding member of the Electric Vehicle Center, this program is part of Toyota’s commitment to developing the next generation of battery engineers and technicians in Michigan.

title: Princeton NuEnergy and SK Battery America Expand Collaboration on US Closed-Loop Battery Recycling - Batteries News
content:
Princeton NuEnergy and SK Battery America Expand Collaboration on US Closed-Loop Battery Recycling
COMMERCE, Ga., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Princeton NuEnergy Inc. (PNE) today announced its ongoing collaboration with SK Battery America (SKBA) to advance the development of a closed-loop recycling pathway for battery manufacturing scrap generated at SKBA’s facilities in Commerce, Georgia.
Under the planned collaboration, PNE will receive battery manufacturing scrap from SKBA. The company is exploring a recycling facility near the manufacturing site to develop a streamlined system for battery materials recycling. Designed to process battery manufacturing scrap, the facility would recover and rejuvenate cathode active material for potential return to battery manufacturing, helping support a more integrated domestic battery supply chain.
PNE recently announced that it has been selected by the U.S. Department of Energy to enter award negotiations for up to $50 million in support of a proposed $110 million project to develop a Cathode-to-Cathode® rejuvenation facility in the United States.
Unlike conventional recycling methods that break battery materials down into their constituent elements, PNE’s direct recycling process is designed to preserve and rejuvenate the engineered structure of cathode materials.
The collaboration reflects PNE and SKBA’s shared interest in improving material circularity, recovering value from battery manufacturing scrap, and strengthening domestic supply chain for critical battery materials. A localized recycling pathway also reduces reliance on imported inputs while supporting U.S. energy security and industrial competitiveness.
PNE and SKBA are continuing discussions regarding the technical and commercial framework for the collaboration.
Chao Yan
, Co-Founder and CEO of PNE, said:
Our business collaboration with SK Battery America reflects growing interest in direct recycling solutions for U.S. battery manufacturing,
“By leveraging PNE’s Cathode-to-Cathode® process, we aim to support a more localized and circular domestic battery materials supply chain.”

title: GM battery material supplier Vianode explores partnership or sale - Batteries News
content:
GM battery material supplier Vianode explores partnership or sale
Vianode looking to fund next expansion phase
Aims to secure partner by year-end, CEO says
Ontario plant could supply synthetic graphite for about 2 million EVs/year
STOCKHOLM, Sept 30 (Reuters) – Norwegian synthetic graphite producer Vianode is seeking a partner to provide capital, industrial ‌expertise or a broader strategic relationship to support its next expansion phase, its CEO Burkhard Straube said.
Vianode, which counts General Motors (GM.N), opens new tab among its customers, is open to outcomes ranging from a partnership to a full takeover, ​Straube told Reuters, adding that the company had hired JP Morgan to help it ​with the process.
Western companies are racing to cut their reliance on China for ⁠battery materials, with Beijing controlling about 95% of global supply of battery-grade graphite.
Vianode hopes to have ​a partner in place as soon as the end of this year and is open to ​industrial and financial investors, Straube said in an interview.
Companies involved in battery manufacturing face a difficult funding environment after the collapse of Sweden’s Northvolt and slowing demand for EVs.
Swedish private equity firm Altor has been Vianode’s sole financial ​backer since 2024, when Norsk Hydro said it would sell its stake and halt further funding.
Straube said ​Vianode, which also has customers in energy storage and defence, needs a new partner to have the same ‌strategic ambitions ⁠and financial capabilities and the capacity to back the company.
Altor spokesperson
Andreas Hamrin
It is an attractive case for the right partner, with Vianode having proven both its technological and commercial viability,
US automaker GM signed a multibillion-dollar agreement in January 2025 for Vianode to provide synthetic ​graphite anode materials for ​EV batteries.
But like Nissan (7201.T), ⁠Jeep maker Stellantis (STLAM.MI
, and others, GM has scaled back its ambitions as demand has cooled and US President Donald Trump has rolled back EV support.
Vianode ​is building a synthetic graphite plant in Ontario capable of supplying material ​for about ⁠2 million EVs annually but requires additional funding for it to be completed.
The company shifted its expansion focus to North America in 2023, arguing Europe lacked the incentives and regulatory support to compete.
Production ⁠is currently ​scheduled to start in 2029, later than originally envisaged.
Vianode ​has operated a plant in Norway since 2024, with capacity expected to reach 2,000 metric tons per year, enough for ​about 35,000 electric vehicles.

title: Arkema invests €10 million in its global battery R&D center of excellence in the Lyon region - Batteries News
content:
Arkema invests €10 million in its global battery R&D center of excellence in the Lyon region
Arkema continues to invest in the battery business value chain and announces a €10 million expansion project for its Global Battery Center of Excellence located in Oullins-Pierre-Bénite, in the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of France.
This investment reflects the Group’s strategy of continuously strengthening its research capabilities in advanced materials for batteries within its global network of R&D laboratories covering the entire battery value chain.
Following the inauguration in Normandy in September 2025 of a laboratory dedicated to solvent-free battery electrode manufacturing, as well as several investments in Asia and the Americas, this expansion further strengthens a particularly dense global R&D network, that combines the expertise developed in France with that of the Group’s research centers in China, South Korea, Japan and the United States. Thanks to this international organization, Arkema is accelerating the development of innovative solutions capable of addressing the technological and industrial challenges of next-generation batteries.
Located at the heart of the Rhône-Alpes Research Center, the Battery Center of Excellence is entering a new phase of its development. Its footprint will be tripled, and its research infrastructure will be modernized, including notably a significant increase in the digitalization of R&D activities. This expansion will consolidate the role of this French center as Arkema’s global reference platform for the development of advanced materials serving both current batteries and the next generations under development.
The project will enable the Group’s R&D teams to prepare for the future industrial standards of cell manufacturers and accelerate the integration of Arkema’s advanced materials into their production processes. By replicating their customers’ manufacturing conditions, researchers will be able to better anticipate implementation constraints and contribute to the development of more efficient batteries delivering greater energy density, faster charging times and enhanced safety.
Armand Ajdari,
Arkema’s Chief technology Officer, said:
This investment marks a major milestone in Arkema’s ambition to support the rapid evolution of the battery market.
”By strengthening our Battery Center of Excellence in France, we are equipping our global network and teams with state-of-the-art tools that will enable them to develop, in close collaboration with our customers, the materials that will contribute to the performance of tomorrow’s batteries.”

title: American Battery Technology Company Receives Approval for Sale of $100 Million of Exported Recycled Black Mass Critical Minerals with License from US Department of Commerce - Batteries News
content:
American Battery Technology Company Receives Approval for Sale of $100 Million of Exported Recycled Black Mass Critical Minerals with License from US Department of Commerce
Significant scale-up of commercial operations at American Battery Technology Company’s domestic U.S. critical mineral recycling facility, demonstrated by its over 400% year-over-year revenue growth and leadership in domestic critical mineral manufacturing
Reno, Nev., Oct. 1, 2026 – American Battery Technology Company (NASDAQ: ABAT), an integrated critical minerals manufacturing company commercializing technologies for both primary critical minerals manufacturing and secondary recycled minerals manufacturing, announced that it has received approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) for the sale of up to $100 million of its recycled black mass material through a license to export under specified terms following the implementation of recently enacted federal export controls governing critical battery materials.
Ryan Melsert,
CEO of American Battery Technology Company, said:
We are grateful for this license and continued support from the U.S. government for the sales of our domestic critical mineral products as we scale both our current critical mineral recycling facility and also our second recycling facility supported by $150 million in competitive grants from the U.S. Department of Energy,
“As demonstrated by the progress reflected in our fiscal year 2026 financial results, we continue to successfully execute on the commercialization of our technologies and expand our role within the critical minerals value chain.”
This Defense Priorities and Allocation System (DPAS) license follows a year of significant commercial and operational progress for American Battery Technology Company (ABTC). As highlighted in the company’s recently reported fiscal year 2026 financial results, ABTC continues to advance the commercialization of its critical mineral recycling technologies, expand customer engagement, and execute against its strategy of building a domestically integrated critical minerals platform. The ability to continue selling exported recycled black mass critical minerals supports current operations, strengthens the company’s market position, and further enhances its ability to capitalize on growing demand for critical minerals across global supply chains.
ABTC currently operates its first commercial-scale critical mineral recycling facility near Reno, Nevada, where it processes end-of-life batteries and manufacturing scrap into strategically recovered materials, including copper, aluminum, steel, lithium-rich intermediates, and black mass. The facility began commercial operations in 2023 and utilizes the company’s internally developed battery recycling technologies.
Black mass contains valuable critical minerals, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese, and graphite, which can be further refined and returned to the critical mineral supply chain for the manufacturing of new products. ABTC has previously emphasized its commitment to supporting the development of a North American closed-loop circular economy through the recovery, recycling, and reuse of critical minerals.
The company remains focused on expanding domestic critical mineral production through both recycling and primary resource development initiatives, helping strengthen U.S. supply chain resilience and support the growing demand for critical minerals essential to electrification, energy storage, and national energy security.

title: Momentum Technologies Names Ben Gilliams Executive Partner, Technology, Operations & Strategy - Batteries News
content:
Momentum Technologies Names Ben Gilliams Executive Partner, Technology, Operations & Strategy
Veteran of Umicore, Redwood Materials, and Nyrstar to help scale Momentum’s commercial critical minerals platform as the company advances its Carrollton, Texas REE line and plans a second
commercial-scale plant
CARROLLTON, Texas, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Momentum Technologies (“Momentum”), a critical minerals refining and recovery company, today announced that Ben Gilliams has been named Executive Partner, Technology, Operations & Strategy. In this role, Gilliams will help guide work across technology and innovation, operations and scale-up, and commercialization and strategic development, while partnering closely with Momentum’s leadership team on key growth priorities.
The appointment expands Gilliams’s role with Momentum as the company enters its next phase of commercial scale-up. Momentum’s first commercial Rare Earth Element (REE) line, which refines recycled hard-disk-drive feedstock under an executed tolling agreement with a hyperscale technology customer, is now operational at Carrollton and ramping toward 300 tons-per-year capacity. A second commercial-scale plant at Carrollton, designed for up to 1,000 tons per year of REE capacity across two build-out phases, is under active development as Momentum prepares for a final investment decision.
Mahesh Konduru,
CEO of Momentum, said:
Ben brings nearly three decades of global operating leadership in critical minerals and advanced materials at exactly the moment Momentum is moving from demonstration to commercial scale,
“Ben has already played an important role in shaping how we scale, and this expanded role reflects both his impact to date and the breadth we need as we bring our second Carrollton plant online. He’s the right person to help us build a platform that lasts.”
A Global Track Record in Critical Minerals and Materials Operations
Gilliams brings close to 30 years of international general management, operations, and technology leadership across the metals, mining, and battery materials industries, with experience spanning Europe, the U.S., and Asia.
Prior to his work with Momentum, Gilliams served as Vice President, Operations and Strategic Projects, Europe at Nyrstar, where he focused on operational and strategic initiatives across the company’s European business. Before Nyrstar, he served as Senior Vice President, Global Strategic Programs at Redwood Materials, where he coordinated upstream strategy, scouted new and complementary technologies, and helped build the processes and footprint for Redwood’s upstream refining and recycling operations.
He also spent more than a decade in senior operating roles at Umicore, including as Vice President of Operations & Process Technology for its Rechargeable Battery Materials business, where he led international sites across Belgium, Finland, and China and served as a board member at two Chinese joint ventures and a wholly owned Finnish operation. Earlier Umicore roles included Vice President of Global Operations & Engineering for Refining & Recycling and Global Business & Technology Director, spanning the company’s cobalt, specialty materials, and precious metals refining businesses across Europe, the U.S., and Asia.
Gilliams
Momentum is at an inflection point that few companies in this industry ever reach: real commercial volumes, a growing pipeline, and a technology platform built for replication,
“I’m excited to broaden my work with the team across technology, operations, and commercialization as we scale what we’ve proven at Carrollton.”
Gilliams holds a Ph.D. in chemistry and a master’s degree in chemistry from the Catholic University of Leuven, and an MBA from Vlerick Business School.
Advancing Momentum’s Commercial Platform
Momentum’s Carrollton demonstration and commercial operations have processed more than 7,000 tons of REE and battery-materials feedstock to date, logging over 1,200 operating hours across two daily shifts. The facility has demonstrated 99.9% purity for Yttrium, 99.5% purity for NdPr Oxide, and battery-grade purity for cobalt and nickel, and Momentum’s technology base now includes six newly filed Momentum process patents alongside four patents licensed from Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The planned second Carrollton plant, together with a growing near-term pipeline of REE and black mass processing opportunities, positions Momentum to significantly expand its domestic processing footprint over the coming year.

title: Ultium Cells to bring LMR prismatic battery cell production to Tennessee for future GM EVs - Batteries News
content:
Ultium Cells to bring LMR prismatic battery cell production to Tennessee for future GM EVs
Spring Hill, Tennessee is blazing a new trail in battery technology, as Ultium Cells LLC – a joint venture between General Motors and LG Energy Solution – just announced plans to produce lithium manganese rich (LMR) prismatic battery cells at its plant just outside Nashville. This is expected to make Ultium Cells the first manufacturer globally to commercially produce this next-generation technology, positioning GM at the forefront of bringing the technology to market in future electric vehicles.
LMR prismatic battery cells mark a major step forward for GM’s future EVs. The technology is designed to offer energy density 33% greater than lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry – today’s leading, low-cost battery technology — but at a comparable cost.
Establishing LMR prismatic cell production at Ultium Cells in Spring Hill is a key step in our strategy to match the right battery technology to customer needs and strengthen our leadership in domestic battery manufacturing and innovation. High-nickel batteries will continue to give customers the highest range in our portfolio, while adding LMR positions us to leapfrog today’s more affordable chemistries and deliver lower costs with better performance. This flexibility allows us to scale efficiently, reach more customers, and support our long-term EV strategy and profitability journey.
Adding LMR to the Ultium Cells portfolio also demonstrates the flexibility of its manufacturing capabilities. Ultium Cells will be able to produce battery cells in multiple chemistries and form factors, helping tailor battery technology to the needs of different vehicles and applications.
Beyond flexing manufacturing might, bringing this new battery cell to market first is a milestone moment for keeping America competitive globally in EV and battery technology leadership.
Construction and facility upgrades at Ultium Cells Spring Hill will begin later this year and are expected to be completed in 2028. This expansion is projected to create 500 new jobs, in addition to the facility’s total current workforce of 1,200 employees.

title: WACKER to Showcase Advanced Silicone Technologies for Thermal Management and Battery Safety at The Battery Show 2026 - Batteries News
content:
WACKER to Showcase Advanced Silicone Technologies for Thermal Management and Battery Safety at The Battery Show 2026
WACKER will highlight silicone technologies for thermal management, thermal runway protection and efficient processing in battery and electronics applications.
Featured technologies span thermally conductive potting, flexible barrier coatings and thermal interface materials for mobility applications.
Material capabilities include customizable thermal conductivity, room-temperature curing, primerless adhesion, flame resistance and ceramic shielding under extreme heat.
ANN ARBOR, Mich., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Wacker Chemical Corporation will showcase advanced silicone technologies for thermal management, thermal protection and processing in battery and electronics applications at The Battery Show 2026. The event takes place Oct. 12-15 at Huntington Place in Detroit, where WACKER will exhibit at Booth 4422. The company will highlight materials for thermally conductive potting and mobility applications as well as a flexible silicone coating that forms a ceramic thermal barrier under extreme heat.
Battery pack design places significant demands on material performance. Thermal management materials must transfer heat effectively while also meeting requirements for dispensing, curing, adhesion, temperature stability and integration into production processes. WACKER’s exhibit will focus on how silicone materials can address those interconnected requirements across battery pack and electronics applications.
Peter Zorney,
WACKER Senior Director of the Electronics and Automotive business segment for North and Central America, said:
Thermal management is closely connected to both battery performance and the manufacturing process
“Engineers have to consider how a material behaves during dispensing and curing, how it performs across operating temperatures and how effectively it supports the application over time while fulfilling increasingly demanding safety requirements. As battery pack architectures continue to develop, that combination of thermal and processing performance becomes increasingly important.”
Thermally Conductive Potting Supports Efficient Processing
WACKER will feature ELASTOSIL® RT 7650 TC VS A/B, a low-viscosity, self-leveling silicone potting compound for battery pack, power and electronics applications. The two-part material offers primerless adhesion, customizable thermal conductivity from 1.2 to 3.0 W/m•K and low sedimentation that supports easy rehomogenization and efficient dispensing.
Flexible Silicone Barrier Responds to Extreme Heat
ELASTOSIL® CM 146 US A/B is a sprayable silicone coating for flexible barrier systems in battery applications. The material remains deformable after curing, then forms a hard ceramic shield at temperatures above 600°C, providing strong thermal insulation during a thermal runaway event. It also offers fast room-temperature curing, low volatile content and no oil bleeding effect.
Thermally Conductive Material Supports Changing Pack Designs
WACKER will also highlight SEMICOSIL® PE 9351 TC VS A/B for assembly applications in automotive battery and electronics manufacturing. The two-component hybrid adhesive material provides thermal conductivity up to 2.0 W/m•K, non-slump dispensing behavior, room-temperature curing and UL 94 V-0 flame-retardant performance. Its processing characteristics support evolving New Electric Vehicle from module-to-pack to cell-to-pack architectures.
The Battery Show brings together scientists, engineers, executives and technology providers across battery and electronic components development value chain, EV technology, manufacturing and safety. The 2026 event will take place Oct. 12-15 at Huntington Place in Detroit. WACKER experts will be available at Booth 4422 to discuss material requirements and silicone technologies for battery and electronics applications.

title: LMATE to Showcase Halogen-Free Flame-Retardant Adhesive Materials for Fast-Charging EV Batteries at Hong Kong Consumer Electronics Show - Batteries News
content:
LMATE to Showcase Halogen-Free Flame-Retardant Adhesive Materials for Fast-Charging EV Batteries at Hong Kong Consumer Electronics Show
SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — South Korean electronic materials company LMATE will participate in the Hong Kong Consumer Electronics Show to present its latest materials for fast-charging EV battery applications and explore partnerships with overseas battery and materials companies for joint application evaluations.
LMATE will present a halogen-free flame-retardant adhesive and a heat-resistant EV battery tape for cell securing and packaging, along with resin coating solutions for the bottom and sidewall surfaces of battery packs.
As charging speeds increase, battery systems face greater thermal loads and must account for the risk of heat propagation within the pack. To address these challenges, LMATE is proposing battery packaging tape for cell securing and packaging, along with resin coating for the bottom and sidewall surfaces of battery packs, as part of its approach to battery thermal propagation mitigation. The materials are designed with heat resistance, flame retardancy and adhesion performance in mind. The halogen-free design offers an alternative to formulations using halogenated flame retardants.
At the core of LMATE’s approach is a reactive design that chemically incorporates flame-retardant functionality into the adhesive resin. The design is intended to reduce the migration, or bleeding, of flame-retardant components and the potential loss of adhesion associated with additive-based formulations.
LMATE’s technical data includes evaluation results for 180-degree peel strength and heat resistance. A specified tape specimen met the UL 94 VTM-0 classification in testing. Actual application performance and regulatory compliance must be verified separately based on substrate type and thickness, operating environment and test conditions.
LMATE also plans to work with customers to evaluate insulation and dielectric properties under the electrical-field and electromagnetic-interference conditions relevant to their cell, module and pack designs. Performance will be assessed for each application and operating environment.
Kim Jung-ryeol,
CEO of LMATE, said:
Materials for faster-charging batteries need to withstand heat, slow flame spread and remain securely bonded,
“We plan to work with customers on application validation that also takes electrical characteristics into account under their actual operating conditions.”
LMATE develops adhesives, bonding materials and coating resins for customized applications in advanced industries, including batteries, semiconductors and displays.

title: Nanoramic Launches Neocarbonix® Slurry Precursor (NXSP™) Standard Product Catalog to Deliver Immediate Cost and Performance Gains for Battery Manufacturers - Batteries News
content:
Nanoramic Launches Neocarbonix® Slurry Precursor (NXSP™) Standard Product Catalog to Deliver Immediate Cost and Performance Gains for Battery Manufacturers
BOSTON, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — September 30, 2026 – Nanoramic, Inc. (“Nanoramic”), an industry leader in advanced materials and energy storage technology, today announced the launch of its standard catalog of Neocarbonix
Slurry Precursor (NXSP™) products. This product line provides battery makers with a scalable, easy-to-implement solution to reduce cost per kWh and improve lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery performance across multiple applications.
NXSP is a drop-in replacement for conventional Li-ion binders and additives in both cathodes and anodes, designed for immediate implementation into existing wet-coating manufacturing lines. By replacing conventional binders and additives with a composite binder, NXSP removes critical constraints on performance, cost, and sustainability without requiring manufacturers to alter their production equipment.
NXSP enables fundamental mechanical and electrochemical performance benefits to cathodes, anodes, and cells across every major application, including electric vehicles (EVs), stationary storage, consumer electronics, drones, and power tools.
NXSP is chemistry-agnostic and seamlessly integrates with various Li-ion cathode chemistries including NCM, NCA, NCMA, LMR, and LFP, and with next-generation technologies such as sodium-ion and solid-state batteries. Across the board, cathodes with NXSP demonstrate higher active material content, higher mass loading, lower resistance, excellent mechanical flexibility, and superior adhesion – driving greater energy density and power density at once, along with meaningful cell cost savings from thicker electrodes and lower processing costs.
NXSP extends the same benefits to silicon anode formulations, overcoming the mechanical degradation and cycle-life instability that silicon volume expansion causes in conventional binder systems. NXSP provides the mechanical flexibility and adhesion needed to sustain performance through repeated charge cycles while improving electrical conductivity, helping manufacturers adopt silicon anodes and move past the energy density limits of conventional graphite anodes.
NXSP is available using raw material inputs sourced to support customers’ own compliance planning under the United States National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) and evolving Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) restrictions on battery materials.
John Cooley,
Founder and CEO of Nanoramic, said,
The release of our standard product catalog was a necessary step to serve the broadening demand we are receiving across all key applications.
”This product standardization along with the mass production capacity we brought online earlier this year positions us for rapid, organic growth.”

Li-Fire Expands Lithium Battery Fire Safety Programs to Help Businesses Scale Protection as Regulations and Risks Grow
Wholesale and distributor programs make proven lithium battery safety solutions more accessible to businesses and industries facing increasing battery-related risks.
PALM BEACH, Fla., Oct. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Li-Fire, one of the leading lithium battery fire suppression solution companies on the market, is celebrating the upcoming National Fire Safety Week by expanding its successful wholesale and distribution program nationwide.
Initially launched to support fire safety equipment companies working closely with fire stations along the East Coast, the company has since worked with a variety of industries across the U.S. to address ongoing lithium battery risks. As a result, its wholesale and distributor program can now support any industry seeking protection from lithium-ion battery incidents, including manufacturing, transportation, logistics, warehousing, energy storage, aviation, technology, universities, and the military.
Bricen Miller
, Founder of Li-Fire, said:
Expanding our wholesale and distribution programs makes it easier for organizations to scale their lithium battery safety efforts alongside operations — particularly in industries where batteries are stored, transported, charged, manufactured, repaired, recycled, or routinely used,
Furthermore, our new expanded programs allow companies to more readily tap into the growing number of fire safety grants and incentives being offered nationwide as part of that process,
The National Fire Protection Association estimates that more than 5,200 lithium-ion battery incidents occur annually in the U.S., and some states have reported up to a 70% increase in lithium battery fire incidents in 2026 alone. From electric vehicles and aviation applications to industrial equipment and energy storage systems, the rapid adoption of lithium-ion battery technology has created new opportunities for businesses while concurrently introducing thermal runaway risks that can be detrimental to companies. As an emerging industry leader, Li-Fire has helped these critical industries implement the right lithium battery fire solutions as part of their overall safety program.

content:
Stryten Energy Completes Acquisition of C&D Trojan, Creating a Leading Battery Manufacturing Platform for Transportation, Industrial, Critical Infrastructure and Military Applications
Creates one of North America’s most comprehensive battery manufacturing and energy storage portfolios serving transportation, golf cart, marine, specialty motive, industrial, critical infrastructure, military and government markets
Establishes a footprint of 15 U.S. manufacturing plants to support American energy independence, industrial resilience and military readiness
Strengthens global presence to better serve customers worldwide through operations in Mexico and China and offices across Europe and AsiaExpands AGM battery manufacturing capacity to meet the growing demand for start-stop and hybrid vehicle applications
ALPHARETTA, Ga.–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Stryten Energy LLC (“Stryten” or “Stryten Energy”) today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of C&D Technologies, Inc. and Trojan Battery Company, LLC (“C&D Trojan”), creating one of North America’s most comprehensive battery manufacturing and energy storage companies, with expanded capabilities across transportation, essential power, industrial, military and government markets.
The combined company operates 18 battery manufacturing and component facilities across the U.S., Mexico and China and employs approximately 4,800 people worldwide, significantly expanding Stryten’s manufacturing scale, global reach and customer support capabilities. The company will continue to operate under the Stryten Energy name while preserving the C&D Technologies and Trojan Battery product brands.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Mike Judd,
Chief Executive Officer and President of Stryten Energy, said:
Today, we are proud to officially welcome the talented employees of C&D Trojan to the Stryten Energy team.
”Together, we bring decades of manufacturing expertise, innovation and customer commitment as one company. We intend to accelerate investments in domestic battery manufacturing capacity, advanced energy storage technologies and military production capabilities, creating a stronger company with the scale, technology portfolio and manufacturing capabilities to support growing customer demand across transportation, specialty motive, data center, telecommunications, industrial and military applications. As we begin this next chapter together, we move forward as
One Company. Powering What’s Possible.
Expanding U.S. Manufacturing
Stryten expects to make strategic investments in U.S. battery manufacturing capacity, facility modernization, equipment upgrades and workforce development. These investments are intended to strengthen domestic production capabilities across advanced lead and lithium battery technologies while supporting long-term American manufacturing competitiveness.
In addition, the company plans to expand its Absorbent Glass Mat (AGM) battery manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand from automotive aftermarket customers for start-stop and hybrid vehicle applications requiring high-performance batteries.
The addition of C&D Trojan significantly expands our ability to serve the automotive aftermarket with advanced AGM battery technology.
”As vehicle electrification continues to evolve, AGM batteries remain a critical technology for start-stop systems, hybrid and advanced electrical loads. By expanding domestic AGM manufacturing capacity, we are strengthening our ability to provide our customers with reliable, high-performance energy storage solutions while reinforcing U.S. battery manufacturing leadership,”
Strengthening Military Production Capacity
The combination of the companies’ military battery portfolios creates one of the most comprehensive domestic battery platforms supporting U.S. defense, government and national security applications. Planned investments will support the scaling of U.S.-based manufacturing capacity to meet increasing demand for batteries used in land warfare systems, air defense systems, Naval surface/undersea systems, logistics, reserve power systems, nuclear power and other essential infrastructure. The combined platform strengthens the domestic industrial base while supporting secure access to mission-critical battery technologies.
Paul Hastings LLP served as legal counsel for Stryten. Jefferies served as financial advisor and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton and Garrison LLP as legal counsel for C&D Trojan.

title: Antora and Pratt Energy Announce Nearly 6 Gigawatt-Hour Thermal Battery Project to Deliver Affordable Energy and Strengthen Kansas Economy - Batteries News
content:
Antora and Pratt Energy Announce Nearly 6 Gigawatt-Hour Thermal Battery Project to Deliver Affordable Energy and Strengthen Kansas Economy
The project, backed by Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners and Grok Ventures, will create high-quality jobs, provide workforce training, and deliver lasting community benefits to Pratt County, Kansas.
PRATT, Kan.–(BUSINESS WIRE)–Antora Energy, a leading U.S. energy storage company, today announced a 5.8 gigawatt-hour, multi-day thermal energy storage project at Pratt Energy’s biorefinery in Pratt, Kansas. Once complete, the project will be one of the largest battery storage systems in the world and deliver affordable, reliable energy to Pratt Energy’s facility, creating jobs and strengthening the local economy.
Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), a global fund manager and leading investor in energy infrastructure, led the project’s third-party equity financing as part of its credit platform investments. Australian investment firm Grok Ventures and University Pension Plan Ontario (UPP) also participated.
Antora’s thermal batteries help meet Kansas’s rising energy demand using locally produced energy, without increasing power bills for homes or businesses. The project is expected to use little additional water beyond the biorefinery’s existing operations and operate without increasing noise levels for neighboring properties. The project is expected to create and support over 100 construction and operations jobs.
This deployment is the second major project Antora has announced this year, following the company’s commissioning of a 5 gigawatt-hour system in Big Stone City, South Dakota. Starting next year, Antora will deliver competitively priced, around-the-clock energy to Pratt Energy under a long-term heat offtake agreement. That locally produced energy will make Pratt’s operations more efficient and its products more competitive. The project will also help Pratt Energy pave the way towards producing 100% zero-carbon-intensity (CI) ethanol, opening new markets for Kansas agricultural products.
David Bierman,
co-founder and Chief Commercial Officer of Antora, shared:
American industry runs on affordable, reliable energy,
“Our partnership with Pratt Energy delivers it, helping meet Kansas’s rising energy demand without increasing power bills for homes or businesses. This biorefinery project is creating jobs and spurring local investment without straining the resources the community depends on.”
Reiner Boehning
, Partner at Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, said:
Antora has demonstrated something rare: sound technology, compelling economic fundamentals, and a clear path to repeatable deployment at scale.
”That gave us the conviction to partner with Antora on this project. Investments like this one provide the energy infrastructure American industry depends on, while delivering real and lasting benefits to the rural communities where these projects are built.”
Travis Lane,
CEO of Pratt Energy, said:
Reliable energy is the foundation of everything we do, and this project lays that foundation for decades to come,
“It means more jobs across the Pratt community, new opportunities for our students, and strengthened demand for the corn and sorghum our neighbors grow. It’s not just an investment in Pratt Energy—it’s an investment in Pratt, Kansas, and everyone who calls it home.”
Antora’s thermal batteries store low-cost electricity as heat in insulated blocks of solid carbon and deliver it around the clock as heat or power. The same factory-built modules can serve a chemical plant, a food producer, a steelmaker, or the grid, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.
Investing in the Pratt Community
Antora has partnered with Pratt Community College on a paid internship program that gives local students hands-on experience with advanced energy and electrical systems. This program is already delivering benefits: two students from the College’s Electrical Powerline Technology program spent this summer working on Antora’s Big Stone project in South Dakota, gaining experience with the same technology now coming to their hometown. Antora will prioritize local candidates as it hires for the plant’s permanent operations roles.
Through a partnership with the South Central Community Foundation (SCCF), Antora is funding an energy scholarship program that will support up to 12 Pratt students over three years as they pursue post-secondary education in energy, engineering, and the skilled trades. Antora is also establishing the Pratt Community Impact Fund, which will provide grants to projects and programs serving Pratt County beginning in 2027. The fund will be administered by SCCF, with grant decisions made by Pratt County community members.
Kyle Farmer,
Mayor of Pratt and a teacher at Pratt High School, said:
Antora came to Pratt early, listened, and followed through on their commitments: local hiring, internships, and scholarships for our students,
“This project brings affordable energy to one of our key employers and ensures steady demand for the grain our farmers produce. We’re proud to welcome Antora to our community.”
Kaleb Reagle,
a recent Pratt Community College graduate who interned at Antora’s Big Stone project this summer and is now a full-time technician at Antora, said:
Seeing what Antora has done for the community in Big Stone and bringing that back to Kansas is really exciting,
“This feels like giving back to the community that raised me. There are students at Pratt right now who were in my spot just a few months ago, and I can’t wait to see what this project opens up for them.”

empower US operations
Supporting critical infrastructure
Michigan LIFT is a public-private initiative designed to support supply chain resilience and increase growth within manufacturing. Around the world, supply chains are disconnected or lack competitiveness, as suppliers cannot always get the financing or workforce needed to scale. As a result, manufacturers cannot always be supported in their own attempt to grow to scale.
The new platform has been created by industry experts in order to
strengthen the competitiveness of manufacturers
and help increase innovation within Michigan-based innovators.
The platform spots challenges that are being faced in manufacturing and supply chain operations, turning them into ‘Open Calls’ so that other suppliers can find solutions. When the solution appears as though it can be widely adopted, Michigan LIFT connects customer demand, financing, public resources, workforce support and commercialisation services.
“Michigan has always been a state that builds, and we’re going to keep leading the next generation of American industry,” explains Governor Gretchen Whitmer.
“Michigan LIFT will bring together our world-class manufacturers, innovative companies, skilled workers and capital to turn big ideas into real products, new investment and good-paying jobs. By working together, we can bring more critical supply chains home, help Michigan businesses grow and show the world that the future is built right here in Michigan.”
The founders of this platform will be playing to individual strengths to help meet expectations.
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer (D-MI)
Plans and priorities:
Ford: the anchor industrial buyer, aims to award up to US$1bn of business to innovate suppliers
JPMorganChase: the founding capital provider, has goals of financing up to US$1bn of debt capital to Michigan LIFT suppliers
State of Michigan, through the Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC): the public-sector participant, using the state’s economic development tools to support innovation-driven companies
Michigan Central: providing the physical testing and scaling environment, offering purpose-built infrastructure and a collaborative platform
Newlab: plans to contribute US$20m of support, with a focus on translating industrial demand into commercialisation opportunities
Michigan Central, Newlab and the Michigan Economic Development Corporation: aim to attract 10–20 additional industrial buyers representing more than US$1bn in annual demand commitments by the end of 2036
Facing modern risks
In today’s world, steady customer demand is uncertain. Volatility, inflation and extreme weather have all had their impacts on how people purchase and when. Because of this volatility, innovative suppliers are often unable to grow to scale.
Alongside this, there is an ageing population and
increasing skills gaps across industries
. There are so many factors that contribute to the inability to grow, but Michigan LIFT is an attempt to tackle those issues while supporting US production of components, critical technologies and growing capabilities.
“For over a decade, Detroit has shown what is possible when business, government and community leaders work together for the long term,” explains Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorganChase.
“Michigan LIFT builds on that same model of public-private collaboration by connecting customer demand, capital and public resources so more companies can grow, more workers can participate and more critical capabilities can scale here in the United States.”
Michigan has proven to be the ideal place for this initiative to begin, as it has a broad supplier base, growing innovation ecosystem and a wealth of talent in the manufacturing industry. Following this, the founders will explore how this opportunity could be applied elsewhere.
Alongside the platform, Ford Philanthropy and JPMorganChase are providing US$550,000 towards Ford: HOPE – a non-profit which
offers job training and education
to those who need it. This nonprofit has an industrial manufacturing training program, upskilling individuals with robotics, welding and manufacturing skills.
Both the platform and the training programme will be strengthening the supplier network and empowering individuals. In doing so, there is expected to be long-term industrial growth within the sector.
Jamie Dimon, CEO at JPMorgan Chase. Credit: JPMorgan Chase
Michigan LIFT is about helping solve real manufacturing challenges faster.
Jim Farley, President and CEO of Ford Motor Company
Developing resilience
The demand-led platform is designed to meet the needs of the people it is aiming to help. It begins with supply chain challenges or manufacturing concerns, relying on Open Calls which industrial buyers identify. In early days, the core challenges will align with the state’s strengths and various priorities.
These include:
Advanced automation and robotics in manufacturing
Focus across battery storage, semiconductors, nuclear energy
Support across aerospace, propulsion
and critical components
Focus on critical minerals mining, processing and recovery
Manufacturing in life sciences
“Michigan LIFT is about helping solve real manufacturing challenges faster,” Jim Farley, President and CEO of Ford Motor Company.
“It connects innovators, suppliers and manufacturers with the support they need to scale. As we gather this week at Ford ACCELERATE to focus on practical solutions for America’s industrial future, Michigan LIFT is one example of how we're taking action to strengthen the Essential Economy and
build a more resilient manufacturing base
The new programme and the grant opportunities will help strengthen manufacturing capabilities and will develop a more resilient supply chain across the US.
Ford CEO Jim Farley. Credit: Ford
Key companies
Ford Motor Company
Ford Motor Company, founded by Henry Ford in 1903, revolutionized manufacturing with the assembly line production method. Headquartered in Dearborn, Michigan, Ford produces automobiles and commercial vehicles under the Ford and Lincoln brands. The company pioneered affordable transportation with the Model T and continues innovating in electric vehicles, autonomous driving technology, and connected services while maintaining its global automotive position.
JPMorganChase
JPMorgan Chase & Co. is America's largest bank and leading global financial services firm. The 2000 merger of JPMorgan and Chase Manhattan created an institution tracing to 1799. Headquartered in New York City, it serves millions worldwide through consumer banking, investment banking, commercial banking, and asset management. The company manages trillions in assets and maintains significant global market influence.
Michigan Economic Development Corporation
The Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC) is the state's primary marketing and business attraction agency. Established to drive job creation and community development, MEDC offers grants, loans, and incentives to businesses. The organization promotes Pure Michigan tourism, supports entrepreneurship and innovation initiatives, and facilitates public-private partnerships. MEDC strengthens Michigan's economy by attracting businesses and helping existing companies expand statewide.
Michigan Central
Michigan Central is a historic Detroit train station in Corktown, built in 1913. After decades abandoned, Ford Motor Company purchased and restored the Beaux-Arts landmark, reopening it as an innovation hub in 2023. The campus focuses on mobility technology, autonomous vehicles, and electric transportation. Michigan Central hosts startups, companies, and community spaces, symbolizing Detroit's revitalization and growth.
Newlab is a Brooklyn-based innovation platform supporting deep-tech startups and corporations on sustainable urban solutions. Founded in 2016, it provides prototyping facilities, workshops, and collaborative workspaces in a former naval shipyard. Newlab focuses on climate technology, mobility, advanced manufacturing, and artificial intelligence. The organization connects entrepreneurs with partners, investors, and resources, fostering collaboration to accelerate transformative technology.

title: Finastra: Driving Visibility With Supply Chain Finance
content:
Finastra: Driving Visibility With Supply Chain Finance
Prioritise Us
on Google
Finastra is working to increase visibility across supply chain finance. Credit: Unsplash
Finastra's new supply chain finance platform is leading to better risk management and visibility, Vinay Mendonca, Finastra’s Head of Product explains
Finastra has launched a platform that connects payables and receivables finance with trade and lending systems through its Nexus API Suite. The software provider announced the solution at Sibos with the aim of helping supply chain professionals access working capital programmes without waiting for banks to build custom infrastructure.
The platform could show how corporate buyers and suppliers might reduce the time needed to onboard counterparties and process invoices. According to Finastra, the system is designed to support straight-through processing across thousands of counterparties and millions of invoices.
Working capital across product lines
Supply chain finance teams often manage payables, receivables and inventory through separate systems. Finastra Supply Chain Finance is intended to create a unified view of working capital exposures across trade finance, lending and supply chain products.
The platform connects with enterprise resource planning systems and external trade ecosystem providers through the Nexus API Suite. Deployment options include on-premise and software-as-a-service models.
The first release covers payables and receivables finance. Future releases are expected to extend into purchase-order finance, pre- and
post-shipment finance, inventory finance
and distributor finance.
Finastra provides financial services software to more than 7,000 customers worldwide, including 80% of the world's top 50 banks.
Performance indicators
Three times more trade-finance deals
95% faster processing
80% reduction in labour costs alongside a 70% uplift in straight-through processing for paperless guarantees
Operational benefits for finance teams
The Finastra Supply Chain Finance platform has already been integrated into operations and alongside other platforms, with banks already seeing unification in their workflow.
Vinay Mendonca, Head of Product, Trade Supply Chain Finance and Corporate Channels at Finastra, tells Supply Chain Digital: "Benefits include increased straight-through processing and a more joined-up approach to working capital and risk management, with
clearer visibility of how credit limits
are being used across products enabling banks to distribute risk more effectively and scale their operations efficiently."
The platform is designed to automate onboarding, fulfilment, servicing and risk management across the programme lifecycle. This could mean treasury and finance teams spend less time on manual processes and reconciliation.
According to Finastra, the system includes AI-enabled fraud detection, compliance screening and eligibility monitoring.
Automated risk distribution
features cover pricing, limit management and reconciliation.
Vinay adds: "Banks are looking for ways to bring new working capital solutions to market faster to capture new revenue streams delivered through STP journeys, and lower costs, while addressing operational risks and regulatory complexity."
Vinay Mendonca, Head of Product, Trade Supply Chain Finance and Corporate Channels at Finastra
Integration with trade systems
The platform works alongside Finastra's Trade Innovation and Loan IQ products. Trade Innovation is a digital trade finance platform designed to automate workflows across letters of credit, guarantees, collections and supply chain finance.
According to Finastra, Trade Innovation has delivered three times more trade finance deals, 95% faster processing and an 80% reduction in labour costs alongside a 70% uplift in straight-through processing for paperless guarantees. The company describes the platform as modular, cloud-ready and API-first.
Loan IQ provides loan origination, transaction management and servicing across corporate and commercial lending. The Nexus layer connects Loan IQ with internal systems, fintech applications and external market platforms.
Vinay says: "By combining
new supply chain finance capabilities
with Trade Innovation and Loan IQ, we are enabling banks to take a more connected approach to working capital."
Reducing complexity for corporates
Supply chain finance creates new revenue opportunities for banks but introduces operational, credit and regulatory complexity. Corporates often face delays when banks lack the infrastructure to launch programmes quickly.
The combined architecture could give supply chain teams a route to access finance without replacing existing systems. This approach is intended to reduce integration friction while creating a common data foundation for limits, exposures and portfolio decisions.
Finastra identifies five principal benefits for banks that could translate into operational gains for supply chain professionals:
faster time to market through pre-built connectivity with corporate systems and ecosystem partners
holistic
working capital management
across trade finance, loans, letters of credit and guarantees
automated risk distribution through pricing, limit management and reconciliation capabilities
AI-enabled fraud detection, compliance screening and eligibility monitoring
support for thousands of counterparties and millions of invoices through straight-through processing.
Banks are now looking to develop a more holistic approach when managing traditional trade operations alongside supply chain finance. This presents
a central challenge
for banks: supply chain finance can create new revenue opportunities, but it also introduces operational, credit and regulatory complexity.
[The platform is] enabling banks to distribute risk more effectively and scale their operations efficiently.
Vinay Mendonca, Head of Product, Trade Supply Chain Finance and Corporate Channels at Finastra
Finastra is headquartered in London, UK. Credit: Getty
Key partners
ING Group is a Dutch multinational banking and financial services corporation headquartered in Amsterdam. Founded in 1991 through a merger, ING operates globally with a strong presence in Europe, Asia, and Australia. The bank focuses on retail and commercial banking, offering savings accounts, mortgages, and investment products. Known for its digital-first approach, ING pioneered online banking services and emphasizes sustainable finance initiatives while serving millions of customers worldwide.
Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) is Malaysia's largest financial services group and Southeast Asia's fourth-largest bank by assets. Established in 1960, it operates across 20 countries with over 2,400 offices. Maybank provides comprehensive banking services including consumer banking, corporate finance, investment banking, and Islamic banking through Maybank Islamic. The group serves over 22 million customers and plays a crucial role in supporting regional economic growth and financial inclusion initiatives.
Bank Negara Indonesia
Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) is one of Indonesia's largest state-owned banks, founded in 1946. As a pioneer of Indonesian banking, BNI offers retail, commercial, and corporate banking services with extensive domestic and international networks. The bank serves millions of customers through thousands of branches and ATMs nationwide. BNI focuses on digital transformation, supporting SMEs, and financing infrastructure projects while maintaining its position as a key driver of Indonesia's economic development.
ODDO BHF
ODDO BHF is a Franco-German financial services group formed from the 2016 merger of ODDO & Cie and BHF-BANK. Headquartered in Paris and Frankfurt, it specializes in private banking, asset management, and corporate finance. The group serves wealthy individuals, institutional clients, and corporations across Europe. With approximately €150 billion in assets under management, ODDO BHF combines French and German banking expertise, offering personalized wealth management and investment solutions.
Marketnode
Marketnode is a Singapore-based digital infrastructure company launched in 2021, backed by SGX Group, HSBC, and Temasek. It develops blockchain-based platforms for fixed income securities and digital asset markets. The platform aims to modernize bond issuance, distribution, and settlement processes, enabling efficient tokenization of financial instruments. Marketnode facilitates interoperability between traditional finance and digital assets, supporting the evolution toward more accessible, transparent, and efficient capital markets in Asia and globally.

title: DHL Supply Chain Expands Operations Across US Health Systems
content:
DHL Supply Chain Expands Operations Across US Health Systems
Prioritise Us
on Google
DHL is increasing visibility across US health systems. Credit: DHL
DHL is working to increase visibility across US health systems amid a period of volatility, explains Jim Saponaro, President LSHC, DHL Supply Chain
Supply chains around the world are facing constant tests, and health systems are just one of the sectors facing increased demand.
Healthcare is a critical supply chain, but an increasingly complex one.
Health systems are facing risin
g costs and ongoing disruption across its global network.
In order to streamline operations, DHL Supply Chain has announced a new logistics solution for the US health system.
Ongoing risks
Modern health systems are a challenge in themselves, with external and internal intricacies meaning modern supply chains are operating differently to traditional ones.
These systems encompass hospitals, physician groups and outpatient facilities, and the new solution is aiming to strengthen possibilities for these groups. The new solution is designed to ensure the movement of critical drugs, supplies and equipment is more accurate, more efficient and more resilient.
DHL will be developing a consolidated service centre in order to bring inventory and medical support activities together, incorporating
dedicated transportation and final-mile delivery
to ensure a better point of connection.
In doing this, goods are travelling through the system at a more efficient pace, with more visibility and control over the transportation. As a result, there are less risks to the shipment and also better time-to-patient delivery.
ongoing product shortages
and supply chain disruptions, end-to-end supply chain visibility is mission-critical for health systems,” explains Jim Saponaro, President Life Science and Healthcare, DHL Supply Chain North America, to Supply Chain Digital.
“Knowing what critical products are available, where they are located and how they are moving across the network helps leaders make more informed decisions and respond quickly as needs change. This level of visibility and control not only strengthens day-to-day operations but can also help health systems build resilience and turn their supply chains into a strategic advantage.”
Jim Saponaro, President Life Science and Healthcare, DHL Supply Chain North America
Key facts
2025 saw a 5.3% inpatient volume increase and a 9.8% outpatient volume increase
Total hospital expenses grew 7.5% in 2025
Expenses for supplies increased by 9.9% in 2025, and 13.6% for drugs
DHL Group has committed €2bn to expand its DHL Health Logistics capabilities by 2030
50% of this commitment is allocated to the Americas
Strain on supply chains
Around the world, the population is ageing. People are living longer, which means hospitals and care providers are navigating a more complex and older patient population. Meanwhile, hospitals are facing ongoing and
regular drug and supply shortages
, as well as rising costs. As a result, patient care logistics are becoming more complex.
According to DHL, inpatient volume increased by 5.3% and outpatient volume grew by 9.8% in 2025. At the same time, hospitals were battling a 7.5% growth in expenses, including 13.6% for drugs and 9.9% for supplies.
Many health systems around the world operate across disconnected networks, locations and providers. The fragmentation which arises can subsequently lead to shortages, duplicate orders and other errors, as leaders do not have full visibility into their systems.
DHL brings its history of managing complex supply chains to introduce greater visibility, reduce complexity and create better coordination across the point of care.
The main solution by DHL is to improve the logistics side of the health system, allowing for better cohesion and greater reliability on delivery, translating to better care from the professionals.
Amid ongoing product shortages and supply chain disruptions, end-to-end supply chain visibility is mission-critical for health systems.
Jim Saponaro, President Life Science and Healthcare, DHL Supply Chain North America
Demand for reliable healthcare is increasing, alongside an ageing population. Credit: DHL
A resilience builder
The solution is a customisable consolidated service centre, which will be a hub for storing, preparing, managing and distributing products throughout the network. With this hub, leaders can better track inventory, strengthen supply chain resilience and ensure hospitals have enough space for patients.
“As hospitals and physician practices become part of larger healthcare networks, visibility across the supply chain becomes increasingly critical,” explains Jim.
DHL’s warehouse management system offers real-time visibility into the network, supporting stock replenishment, inventory positioning and constant improvement. This leads to standardisation within purchasing and better control across the supply chain network.
Health supply chains are increasingly introducing
AI, robotics and automation
into their operations, making improvements to accuracy and efficiency in warehouses and service centres.
Alongside the increasing role of technology, DHL’s investments are going a long way for making a more resilient supply chain. DHL Group’s Strategy 2030 places life sciences and healthcare as a strategic growth initiative.
The Group has committed €2bn
(US$2.26bn) to expand its DHL Health Logistics capabilities by 2030, and 50% of it will be going to the Americas. Its East Coast Center of Excellence, a one-million-square-foot life sciences and distribution centre in Annville, has been fully constructed. Alongside this it has acquired CRYOPDP, a specialty courier which oversees clinical trials, biopharmaceuticals and cell and gene therapies.
These investments reflect a strong focus on the healthcare supply chain, with the aim of developing resilience and ensuring it can continue to save as many lives as possible.
DHL is integrating technology and AI into its healthcare supply chains. Credit: DHL
Key companies
DHL Supply Chain
Global leader in contract logistics and supply chain management, DHL Supply Chain operates across multiple sectors including life sciences and healthcare. The company provides end-to-end logistics solutions encompassing warehousing, transportation, and value-added services. With advanced technology integration including AI, robotics, and real-time tracking systems, DHL Supply Chain manages complex networks for healthcare systems, ensuring critical medical supplies reach patients efficiently and reliably.
DHL Health Logistics
Specialized division of DHL Group focused exclusively on healthcare and life sciences supply chains, DHL Health Logistics manages pharmaceutical distribution, medical device logistics, and clinical trial materials. Under DHL Group's Strategy 2030, the division is receiving €2 billion investment by 2030, with 50% allocated to Americas expansion. The division operates specialized facilities including the one-million-square-foot East Coast Center of Excellence.
Specialty courier company acquired by DHL to enhance its life sciences capabilities, CRYOPDP specializes in time-critical and temperature-sensitive logistics for clinical trials, biopharmaceuticals, and advanced cell and gene therapies. The acquisition strengthens DHL's cold chain infrastructure and expands its ability to serve the growing biotech sector requiring ultra-precise handling, storage, and transportation across North America's healthcare network
